subtitle: 只看一眼，真的只看一眼
sentences: The moment A-Qin finished saying, "They're moving the old crates tonight," Wen Li and I turned and ran straight back to the Ministry of Punishments.
Just before we reached the steps, she caught my arm and pulled me back.
"Catch your breath first."
"By the time I finish catching it, those crates will be halfway out of the city!"
"If you charge in like that, Lord Gu will think someone's chasing us with a knife."
I leaned against a veranda pillar and managed two breaths. "That might actually help. At least he'd send a couple of constables straightaway."
Wen Li didn't laugh. She turned to A-Qin. "Who heard this? Where? And does she remember who said it?"

A-Qin rubbed her fingers together nervously. "Auntie Yuan was collecting her pay at the provisions gate when she heard two stewards talking. She didn't dare linger. All she caught was 'Du's,' 'old crates,' and 'finished loading before the third watch.'"
"She didn't hear where they were going?"
"No."
I was about to point out that we had precious little to go on when the duty-room door opened.
Gu Huaichuan stood there with an armful of case files. "Miss Jiang, last time you promised to take just one look. Are you planning to carry off just one crate this time?"
"Lord Gu, must you always assume the worst of me?"
"Every time you come here, the situation is worse than the last."
I decided to let that one go.

Wen Li explained where the note had come from and exactly what Auntie Yuan had overheard, without leaving out which parts were only guesses. As Gu listened, he had a clerk record the information as a possible witness lead.

"I can send men to watch the traffic on the western road," he said, "and ask my superior to authorize an inspection of Du's original lease register as soon as possible. But someone saying crates will be moved tonight doesn't give me grounds to enter private property and break open boxes. For all we know, those 'old crates' really contain millstones and worthless ledgers."
"And what if they burn them tonight?" I asked.
"Which is why we need to track where the wagons go, who escorts them, and whether there are hire records or gate-passage entries."
"What about us?"
"You go home."
"But Wen Li and I can recognize—"
"Home."
Then Gu turned suddenly to A-Qin. "Is Auntie Yuan still at the marquis's residence today?"
A-Qin nodded.
"Tell her to stop asking questions for now. Sending medicine through intermediaries has already drawn attention. Don't sacrifice both Granny Zhou and Auntie Yuan over a few crates."
That got through to me.
After leaving the duty room, Wen Li and I stood at the foot of the steps for a long while.
"Are we really going home?" I asked.
"To your house first."
"And then?"
"We find Uncle Qin."
I stared at her. "Didn't you just give Gu Huaichuan your word?"
"He said not to break into the mill. I have no intention of doing that."
"Then what do you need Uncle Qin for?"
"Your family used to run shipping routes. Surely you know who recognizes wagons better than anyone?"
I thought for a moment, and a light began to dawn.
"Drivers."
"And the people who feed their horses."
"Wen Li," I said with newfound respect, "you are starting to sound exactly like my mother."
"Is that meant to be a compliment?"
"In the Jiang household, it's the highest praise there is."
Half an hour later, Uncle Qin listened to our plan and asked only one question. "Where do you two ladies intend to sit and watch?"
"The tea stall beside the western road," Wen Li replied. "People might recognize me, so we shouldn't get too close."
"The stall is closed tonight."
"Then—"
"The owner is my cousin," Uncle Qin added at his own leisurely pace. "I'll have him open it."
I gave him a look. "Uncle Qin, have you learned to leave people hanging too?"
"From you, miss."

After dark, only one small oil lamp burned in the tea stall. We sat behind a bamboo curtain with three bowls of steaming noodle soup on the table. Uncle Qin had us change into ordinary clothes and forbade us from bringing a Jiang carriage. Wen Li pinned up her hair without fuss. I tried to copy her and stabbed myself twice with the hairpin.
"Could you hold still?" She reached over and redid my hair. "At this rate, they'll have finished moving the crates while you're still fighting your own head."
"I'm nervous, all right?"
She tightened the hair ribbon, but her eyes never left the road.
"So am I."
I blinked. Wen Li had said it so softly it was almost as though she hadn't wanted me to hear.

Two unfamiliar men were sitting in the stall as well. One was chewing flatbread; the other held an empty tea bowl. Uncle Qin hadn't told me who they were, but half a Ministry of Punishments badge showed beneath one man's cuff. I had the sense not to say hello.
Around the second night watch, the first wagon appeared in the distance.
A gray canopy. Two mules. A strip of red cloth hanging at the back.
I nearly sprang to my feet, but Wen Li pressed a hand onto my shoulder.
"Just watch."

The wagon rolled past the stall, its wheels hitting a puddle and throwing up a great splash of mud. There really were wooden crates stacked on it, but they were covered too tightly for us to see inside. Two more wagons followed. One wheel on the second had a crooked strip of replacement iron.
I drew a quiet breath.
A worker at Cen's hauling agency had mentioned that the gray-canopied wagon that took Yan Mancang away also had trouble with its right rear wheel.
"Could it be the same one?" I whispered into Wen Li's ear.
"There's no way to tell. Repairs can change how a wheel looks."
She wouldn't let my guess turn into a conclusion.
At the fork in the road, the three wagons split up. Two headed north; the third turned toward the river wharf.
The man eating flatbread rose abruptly and went out without even taking his bowl. The other left some money on the table and followed a little later.
So they had a plan in place all along.
"Gu Huaichuan is pretty reliable after all," I said.
"Tell him that to his face tomorrow."
"Absolutely not. He'll think I'm trying to get out of the paperwork again."
We could have gone home then. Uncle Qin had already asked the owner to put out the lamp.
But just then, an empty mule cart came from the direction of the mill and stopped outside the stall.
Its driver was a tall, thin man with an old scar across his face. He jumped down to ask for water, and as his sleeve rode up, I saw a dark red cord knotted around his wrist.
Wen Li seized my hand.
Her nails almost dug into my palm.
"What's wrong?"
"He's been to the Wen residence."
"When?"
"The day before the wedding." Her voice tightened. "He said he was delivering Xie Linzhou's gift list. I never saw him myself. A-Qin received it."
The thin man finished his water and turned to leave. I had a sudden urge to run after him and demand to know who he was. Wen Li pulled me back before I could move.
"You promised."
I stopped dead.

Uncle Qin had already stepped outside. Smiling, he exchanged a few words with the driver and casually pointed at the cart's shaft. The man answered with some irritation, climbed back aboard, and drove away.
By the time Uncle Qin returned, his smile was gone.
"He says the cart isn't his. Steward Zhao at Nanping Wharf hired it. His job today was to take it to the river landing and bring it back once the loading was done."
"He actually told you that?" I asked.
"I asked why he kept using a cracked shaft instead of replacing it. He was afraid I'd tell someone, so he hurried to explain it was a hired cart. A few extra words, and he let slip who'd rented it."
Wen Li looked down the road where the cart had disappeared.
"Steward Zhao," she repeated.

I remembered that name too. The two hundred taels my mother had accepted had come through a man surnamed Zhao. He was also the one who had tried to get her to alter the delivery receipt all those years ago.
It was a lead, but still nowhere near proof that would justify an arrest.
I was about to speak when Uncle Qin pushed my bowl toward me. "Your noodles are getting cold. Eat first."
"At a time like this, you still want me to eat?"
"Going hungry won't bring those carts back."
I had no choice but to pick up my chopsticks.
Halfway through my noodles, hurried hoofbeats sounded outside the stall. A young constable rode up through the rain. Without coming inside, he asked Uncle Qin to step out and speak with him.
Uncle Qin came back wearing a strange expression.
"Lord Gu sent word. All three wagons have been followed. Two went into an old storehouse to the north, and one stopped at the river wharf. They haven't been able to inspect the cargo yet."
"So we watched all that for nothing?"

"No." Uncle Qin hesitated. "There was a scene outside the Ministry tonight. A man announced in front of a crowd that he wanted to turn himself in. He claimed he'd rewritten the supplementary grain-receipt register for the Northern River case three years ago. Several onlookers heard him say it."
Wen Li looked up sharply.
"What's his name?"
"Ma Shiquan. He used to work as a clerk under your father."
Had I seen that name in the original novel? I racked my brains until my head hurt, but nothing came back to me.
"Why come forward now?" Wen Li asked.
Uncle Qin shook his head. "According to the messenger, the man shouted in public that he'd altered the old register. How much of that is true is for the Ministry to establish."
"Who told him to alter it?"
All at once, the rain grew louder.
Uncle Qin glanced at Wen Li, as if weighing whether he ought to say it. In the end, he did.
"Ma Shiquan shouted that Lord Wen had ordered him to change the amount received at the granary from three thousand shi to eight thousand."
I looked at Wen Li without thinking.
She sat motionless, still holding her bowl of soup.
A long time passed before she set it down. When she finally spoke, her voice was barely above a whisper.
"My father did... write him a letter back then."
translations: 阿芹说完“今夜要把旧箱子挪走”，我和温梨就掉头往刑部跑。
跑到台阶前，她忽然一把拉住我。
“先把气喘匀。”
“再喘，箱子都搬到城外去了！”
“你这样冲进去，顾大人会以为有人追杀我们。”
我扶着廊柱喘了两口：“有人追杀倒好了，他至少能先派两个衙役。”
温梨没笑。她看了一眼阿芹：“这话是谁听见的？在什么地方？还记不记得是谁说的？”
阿芹紧张得直揉手指：“袁婶去采买门领钱，听两个管事说的。她不敢多站，只听见‘杜记’、‘旧箱子’，还有‘三更前装完’。”
“没听见往哪儿送？”
“没有。”
我正要说这还不够，值房的门先开了。
顾怀川抱着一摞卷宗站在门口：“姜姑娘，上回你说只看一眼，这回是不是打算只搬一箱？”
“顾大人，您这人怎么净往坏处想？”
“因为你每次来，事情都比上次严重。”
我决定先不跟他计较。
温梨把纸条的来历和袁婶听见的话讲清楚，连哪些是猜的也没省。顾怀川一边听，一边叫书吏另记口供线索。
“我能派人去西郊官道上看车马出入，”他说，“也会请上官尽快核准查阅杜记的租契原簿。但旁人说今晚搬箱，不足以让我闯进私家院子开箱搜查。何况‘旧箱子’里可能真是磨盘和破账。”
“那若他们今晚烧了呢？”我问。
“所以得盯住车往哪儿走，谁押车，能否查到租车和过关的记录。”
“我们呢？”
“你们回家。”
“我跟温梨都认得——”
“回家。”
顾怀川说完，忽然又转向阿芹：“那位袁婶今日还在侯府？”
阿芹点头。
“先别叫她再打听。你们托人送药的事已经惹眼了，别为了几只箱子把周嬷嬷和袁婶都赔进去。”
这句我听进去了。
从值房出来，我和温梨在台阶下站了很久。
“真回家？”我问。
“先回你家。”
“然后呢？”
“找秦叔。”
我望着她：“你刚才不是答应了顾怀川？”
“他说不准闯磨坊。我也没打算闯。”
“那你找秦叔做什么？”
“你家做过船运，难道还不知道什么人最认得车？”
我想了想，突然有点明白。
“车夫。”
“还有替车夫喂马的人。”
“温梨。”我肃然起敬，“你现在像极了我娘。”
“这是夸我？”
“在姜家，这是最高的夸奖。”
半个时辰后，秦叔听完我们的主意，先问了一句：“二位姑娘准备坐在哪里看？”
温梨说：“西郊官道旁的茶棚。有人认得我，不宜靠太近。”
“茶棚今晚不开。”
“掌柜是我表兄。”秦叔慢悠悠接着说，“我叫他开。”
我看着他：“秦叔，你讲话也学会大喘气了？”
“跟小姐学的。”
入夜后，茶棚只点了一盏豆油灯。我们坐在竹帘后面，桌上摆着三碗热汤面。秦叔让我们换了平常衣裳，没许带姜家的车。温梨把头发简单挽起，我学着她的样子，结果簪子戳了自己两回。
“你能不能别动？”她伸手替我重新盘好，“人家搬完箱子，你还在跟头发较劲。”
“我这不是紧张么。”
她系紧发带，目光却一直望着官道。
“我也是。”
我怔了一下。温梨说得很轻，像是不想让我听见。
茶棚里还坐着两个陌生男人，一人啃饼，一人端着空茶碗。秦叔没告诉我他们是谁，但其中一个袖口露出半截刑部的腰牌。我便识趣地没打招呼。
大约二更时，远处来了第一辆车。
灰篷，双骡，车后挂一块红布。
我差点站起来，被温梨按住肩膀。
“先看。”
车子越过茶棚，车轮压进水洼，溅起半尺泥。车上堆的确实是木箱，但盖得严实，看不清里面。后头又跟来两辆，第二辆轮子有一道歪斜的补铁。
我轻轻吸了口气。
岑记伙计提过，那辆接走严满仓的灰篷车，右后轮也有毛病。
“是不是同一辆？”我贴着温梨耳朵问。
“看不准。车子修过之后也会变样。”
她没有顺着我的猜测往下说。
三辆车行到岔路口，竟分成了两路。前两辆往北，一辆拐去了河埠头。
茶棚里啃饼的男人忽然起身，连碗都没拿就出了门。另一人将钱放在桌上，隔了片刻才跟出去。
原来他们早有安排。
“顾怀川还是挺靠谱的。”我说。
“你明日当面夸他。”
“那不行。他会以为我又想省手续。”
我们原本可以就此回去。秦叔也已经招呼掌柜收灯了。
偏偏这时，最后一辆空骡车从磨坊方向过来，在茶棚门前停下。
赶车的是个瘦高男人，脸上有一道旧疤。他跳下车讨水，袖子一抬，露出手腕上一条暗红色的绳结。
温梨忽然抓住我的手。
她的指甲几乎掐进我掌心。
“怎么了？”
“他来过温府。”
“什么时候？”
“大婚前一天。”温梨声音发紧，“他说来送谢临舟的礼单。我没见他，是阿芹接的。”
瘦高男人喝完水，转身要走。我脑子一热，差点追出去问他究竟是谁。温梨却先把我往后拉了一步。
“你答应过。”
我硬生生停住。
秦叔已经走到棚外，笑着同赶车人说了两句话，顺手指了指那辆车的车辕。男人不耐烦地应了几声，上车走了。
秦叔回来时，脸上笑意早没了。
“他说车不是自家的，是南平码头的赵管事雇的。今日只负责送去河埠，装完就回来。”
“他肯说？”我问。
“我问他车辕为何裂了还舍不得换。他怕我说出去，急着解释车是借来的。多说两句，就漏了租车的人。”
温梨看向那辆车消失的方向。
“赵管事。”她重复了一遍。
我也记得这个名字。我娘收过的那两百两，是姓赵的经手人送来的；当年要她改回执的，也是那个人。
这是一条线，却还不是能抓人的证据。
我刚想开口，秦叔已经把碗推过来：“面快凉了。先吃。”
“这么大的事还吃？”
“你饿着肚子也不能把马车追回来。”
我只好拿起筷子。
汤面吃到一半，茶棚外忽然响起急促的马蹄。一个年轻衙役冒雨赶来，没进门，只叫秦叔到门外说话。
秦叔回来时，脸色有些怪。
“顾大人派人来报，三辆车都跟上了。两辆进了北边旧库，一辆停在河埠头，搬的东西暂时没法查验。”
“那不就白看了吗？”
“不是。”秦叔顿了顿，“刑部门口今晚闹出了动静。有人当着一群人的面喊着要投案，说三年前北河那份收粮副册，是他补写的。几个看热闹的都听见了。”
温梨猛地抬头。
“叫什么？”
“马世全。以前在你父亲手底下做书办。”
这名字我在原著里见过吗？我拼命想，想得脑仁都疼，也没想起来。
“他为什么现在才来？”温梨问。
秦叔摇头：“听街口报信的说，那人当众喊着自己改过旧册；到底有多少真话，还得让刑部查。”
“是谁让他改的？”
雨声忽然变大。
秦叔看了温梨一眼，似乎在犹豫该不该讲。最后他还是开口了。
“马世全当着人喊，是温大人吩咐他把入仓的三千石，改成八千石。”
我下意识看向温梨。
她端着汤碗，一动不动。
过了许久，她才把碗放下，声音很轻。
“我爹当年……确实给他写过一封信。”

annotations.explain: The moment 可引导时间状语从句，突出两件事紧接发生；也可用 the instant 替换。
annotations.example: The moment she called, I left.

annotations.explain: turn and do 是连贯动作，不一定译成两个独立句子；这里表现反应迅速。
annotations.example: He turned and walked out.

annotations.explain: straight 作副词，强调中途没有绕路或停留。
annotations.example: We drove straight back to town.

annotations.explain: catch someone's arm 在叙事中指及时拉住或拦住某人，不是“接住手臂”。
annotations.example: She caught his arm before he stepped off the curb.

annotations.explain: pull somebody back 可以指实际拉回，也可比喻阻止冲动行动。
annotations.example: A friend pulled me back from the edge.

annotations.explain: catch one's breath 是高频固定表达，既可指跑步后平复呼吸，也可指受到惊吓后恢复。
annotations.example: Give me a minute to catch my breath.

annotations.explain: By the time 从句指出后续动作发生的参照时间，主句常强调某事届时已经完成。
annotations.example: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.

annotations.explain: halfway 表示“在半途”，这里用夸张口吻强调耽误不起。
annotations.example: We were halfway out of the city when it started raining.

annotations.explain: charge in 表示不顾周围情形地冲入，常带莽撞意味。
annotations.example: Don't charge in before you know what's happening.

annotations.explain: like that 在句尾指前文的方式或状态，可用于责备和提醒。
annotations.example: You can't speak to her like that.

annotations.explain: lean against something 是身体动作搭配，注意介词 against。
annotations.example: He leaned against the wall.

annotations.explain: At least 用来提出一个最低限度的好处或标准，这里带自嘲意味。
annotations.example: At least we know where to start.

annotations.explain: straightaway 与 right away 近义，英式英语中较常见。
annotations.example: Please call me straightaway if anything changes.

annotations.explain: 否定动作的简短句用于突出人物态度改变，不能机械理解为“她不懂幽默”。
annotations.example: He didn't laugh at the joke.

annotations.explain: turn to somebody 可指转过身体朝向对方，也可表示向对方求助，须结合上下文。
annotations.example: She turned to the witness and asked a question.

annotations.explain: 间接提问放在直接问句结构中，does 为疑问助动词，后接动词原形 remember。
annotations.example: Does he remember where he put the keys?

annotations.explain: 动作描写常借具体肢体语言表现紧张，不必直接使用 nervously 以外的情绪词。
annotations.example: He rubbed his hands together while waiting.

annotations.explain: collect one's pay 比 get paid 更强调亲自去领取款项。
annotations.example: She went to the office to collect her pay.

annotations.explain: dare 后可接动词原形或 to do；linger 指比必要时间停得更久。
annotations.example: He didn't dare linger near the gate.

annotations.explain: catch 在此是“听清、捕捉到”的意思，all ... was 强调信息有限。
annotations.example: All I caught was her last name.

annotations.explain: before 引出截止时间；the third watch 是传统夜间时辰名称，不等于现代固定的某个整点。
annotations.example: They had to finish before midnight.

annotations.explain: 这是间接疑问结构，使用陈述句语序 where they were going，而不是 where were they going。
annotations.example: Do you know where they are going?

annotations.explain: be about to do 强调动作几乎马上发生，经常与 when 连用表示被打断。
annotations.example: I was about to leave when the phone rang.

annotations.explain: precious 修饰 little 不是“珍贵”，而是强调数量非常少，常带讽刺。
annotations.example: We had precious little time to prepare.

annotations.explain: have something to go on 指拥有足以推断或推进调查的依据。
annotations.example: We don't have much to go on yet.

annotations.explain: an armful of 表示双臂能抱住的一大堆物品，文学描写中常见。
annotations.example: He walked in with an armful of books.

annotations.explain: carry off 在此是“搬走”，其他语境中还可指“成功完成困难之事”。
annotations.example: They carried off several boxes.

annotations.explain: assume the worst of someone 指总把某人的动机往坏处想。
annotations.example: Don't assume the worst of your colleagues.

annotations.explain: than the last 省略了 situation / time，避免重复，是英语比较结构的自然写法。
annotations.example: Each storm was worse than the last.

annotations.explain: let something go 可表示放下争执、不追究某句话，语气口语化。
annotations.example: I could have argued, but I let it go.

annotations.phrase: where the note had come from
annotations.explain: 过去完成时 had come 交代比叙述时更早发生的来源事件；where 引导宾语从句。
annotations.example: They asked where the money had come from.

annotations.explain: leave out 表示遗漏或故意省去信息；without + -ing 说明做事方式。
annotations.example: She explained it without leaving out the awkward details.

annotations.explain: only 限制证据等级，提醒读者猜测与事实不可混淆。
annotations.example: Those are only guesses, not confirmed findings.

annotations.explain: have somebody do something 是使役结构，have 后接宾语和动词原形。
annotations.example: The manager had an assistant check the figures.

annotations.explain: watch 在此是持续监视交通流向，并非单纯“看交通”。
annotations.example: Officers watched the traffic at the bridge.

annotations.explain: authorize 是正式授权，inspection 是查验；提出申请不代表已经获批。
annotations.example: The director authorized an inspection of the records.

annotations.explain: 常用时间表达，可缩写 ASAP，但小说对白一般不必写缩写。
annotations.example: Send me the details as soon as possible.

annotations.explain: grounds 指法律或事实依据，give someone grounds to do 强调行为需有正当理由。
annotations.example: The report gave us grounds to investigate further.

annotations.explain: 表示由于信息不足，某种解释仍然可能成立，不是“我们知道所有事情”。
annotations.example: For all we know, they may already have left.

annotations.explain: What if ...? 常用于提出风险情境，语气可担忧也可质疑。
annotations.example: What if the road is closed?

annotations.explain: Which 指代前一句提到的整个情况，引出推理结果，口语里常独立成句。
annotations.example: The forecast is bad, which is why we're staying in.

annotations.explain: track 表持续追查路线，where 后接陈述语序的宾语从句。
annotations.example: We need to track where the package went.

annotations.explain: whether 引导间接的是非疑问，可和 or not 搭配，语义比 if 更明确。
annotations.example: Check whether there are any receipts.

annotations.explain: What about + 名词 / 代词用于把话题转到某人某事，也可以询问安排。
annotations.example: Everyone has a seat. What about us?

annotations.explain: can 表示能力，不表示已经成功认出；未说完的话用破折号模拟被打断。
annotations.example: I can recognize his handwriting.

annotations.explain: for now 强调现阶段安排可能之后改变，不等于永远禁止。
annotations.example: Let's leave the question aside for now.

annotations.explain: through 可表示“经由某种渠道”，intermediary 是中间传递者。
annotations.example: They negotiated through intermediaries.

annotations.explain: draw attention 是固定搭配；have drawn attention 是现在完成时，说明影响延续至今。
annotations.example: The unusual payment has drawn attention.

annotations.explain: over 可表示“因为、就……这件事”，经常暗示代价与原因不成比例。
annotations.example: They argued over a small mistake.

annotations.explain: get through to somebody 表示使对方真正理解或接受某个道理，不是电话接通的意思。
annotations.example: Her warning finally got through to him.

annotations.explain: at the foot of the steps/mountain 是常见地点表达。
annotations.example: They waited at the foot of the stairs.

annotations.explain: a while 是一段时间，加 long 强调持续较久。
annotations.example: No one spoke for a long while.

annotations.explain: give somebody one's word 是严肃但常见的承诺表达，不表示提供一句话。
annotations.example: I gave her my word that I would return.

annotations.explain: have no intention of + -ing，注意介词 of 后接动名词。
annotations.example: I have no intention of changing the plan.

annotations.explain: used to + 动词原形表示过去经常或曾经如此、现在可能已不同，区别于 be used to + -ing。
annotations.example: He used to run a small bookstore.

annotations.explain: 比较级 + than anyone (else) 用于强调某人最擅长某事。
annotations.example: She knows this town better than anyone.

annotations.explain: a light dawns 是领悟的比喻，dawn 也可指“黎明到来”。
annotations.example: A light dawned when she saw the receipt.

annotations.explain: newfound 常作前置形容词，表示刚刚获得或产生的感受。
annotations.example: He spoke with newfound confidence.

annotations.explain: sound like somebody 描述语气风格相似，starting to 表示变化刚开始。
annotations.example: You're starting to sound like your father.

annotations.explain: be meant to be 在此表示“原本打算当作”，不要与命中注定混为一谈。
annotations.example: Was that meant to be funny?

annotations.explain: the highest + 名词形成最高级评价，此处用家庭文化解释反讽。
annotations.example: Coming from her, that's the highest praise.

annotations.explain: intend to 比 want to 更强调经过考虑的计划。
annotations.example: Where do you intend to wait?

annotations.explain: beside 表示“在旁边”，不同于 besides“此外”。
annotations.example: The stall stands beside the road.

annotations.explain: get + 形容词表示状态变化，too 表示超过合适程度。
annotations.example: Don't get too close to the fire.

annotations.meaning: 按他自己的慢悠悠节奏
annotations.explain: at someone's pace 是常用搭配，leisurely 指不紧不慢，这里制造喜剧停顿。
annotations.example: She finished the story at her own leisurely pace.

annotations.explain: have somebody do 为使役结构；him 为宾语，open 为动词原形。
annotations.example: I'll have someone unlock the door.

annotations.explain: leave somebody hanging 指故意把话说到一半让对方等下文，常见口语表达。
annotations.example: Don't leave me hanging—what happened next?

annotations.explain: 省略句 From you, miss 完整意思是 I learned it from you，利用简短回答制造反击。
annotations.example: Where did you hear that? From my brother.

annotations.explain: after dark 是固定时间表达，不需加 the。
annotations.example: We avoid that road after dark.

annotations.explain: behind 表示位于遮挡物后侧，描写隐蔽观察的位置。
annotations.example: They sat behind a screen.

annotations.explain: forbid somebody from doing something 是常见结构，过去式 forbade。
annotations.example: The rules forbid visitors from taking photos.

annotations.explain: without fuss 强调不慌乱也不麻烦别人，常用于评价熟练行动。
annotations.example: She packed without fuss.

annotations.explain: 刺戳自己是一种动作喜剧，stab 在此指簪子不慎扎到，不是遭受攻击。
annotations.example: I pricked my finger with a needle.

annotations.explain: hold still 表示保持身体不动，常用于整理头发、拍照或诊察。
annotations.example: Hold still while I fix your collar.

annotations.explain: At this rate 用于根据当前进度推断令人担忧或好笑的结果。
annotations.example: At this rate, we'll miss the train.

annotations.explain: 这里的 fighting 是幽默夸张；英语可把困难动作比喻成与某物搏斗。
annotations.example: I'm still fighting with this knot.

annotations.explain: 句尾 all right 可表示不耐烦的解释、确认或安抚，需按语气理解。
annotations.example: I'm trying my best, all right?

annotations.explain: eyes never left something 是凝视的固定叙事表达，并非眼睛字面离开。
annotations.example: Her eyes never left the doorway.

annotations.explain: so + 助动词/be + 主语 表示肯定附和，结构倒装；am 对应前句 I'm nervous。
annotations.example: I'm exhausted. So am I.

annotations.explain: as though 引导比较或假设感受，almost 让判断更委婉。
annotations.example: She spoke almost as though she knew the answer.

annotations.explain: as well 通常放句尾，语气比 too 略书面。
annotations.example: Two friends came as well.

annotations.explain: beneath 表示“在下方”，比 under 稍带叙事书面色彩。
annotations.example: A note was hidden beneath his coat.

annotations.explain: have the sense to do 指懂得采取明智行动，not to 表示知趣地克制。
annotations.example: He had the sense not to interrupt.

annotations.explain: 固定介词短语，常搭配 appeared / saw / heard。
annotations.example: We saw a light in the distance.

annotations.explain: 现在分词 hanging 作后置修饰，说明布条的位置和状态。
annotations.example: There was a tag hanging at the back.

annotations.explain: spring to one's feet 是形象化动作搭配，spring 的过去式 sprung 或 sprang。
annotations.example: She sprang to her feet at the news.

annotations.explain: press something onto something 表示施加压力，onto 指向接触面。
annotations.example: He pressed a hand onto the table.

annotations.explain: just 在祈使句中限制行动范围，意思是“只看，别采取其他行动”。
annotations.example: Just listen before you decide.

annotations.explain: roll past 常用于轮式车辆从某处经过，突出平稳滚动。
annotations.example: A wagon rolled past the gate.

annotations.explain: throw up 除“呕吐”外还能描述水、尘土被卷起，必须依据上下文判断。
annotations.example: The wheels threw up mud.

annotations.phrase: too tightly for us to see
annotations.explain: too + 形容词 + for somebody to do 表示程度过高以致无法做某事。
annotations.example: The writing was too small for me to read.

annotations.explain: crooked 可指物体弯斜，也可比喻“不诚实的”，此处是字面描述。
annotations.example: A crooked strip of metal held it together.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时用于从茶棚观察时点回溯此前听来的信息。
annotations.example: She had mentioned the problem earlier.

annotations.explain: have trouble with something 指处理某物困难或某物故障。
annotations.example: We had trouble with the rear wheel.

annotations.explain: could 在此表达不确定推测，而不是过去的能力。
annotations.example: Could it be the wrong address?

annotations.explain: 固定表达，强调现有信息不足，而不是断定绝不可能知道。
annotations.example: There's no way to tell from this photo.

annotations.explain: how 引导间接疑问或方式从句，用陈述句语序。
annotations.example: Lighting can change how a room looks.

annotations.explain: turn something into something 表示把某物转化为另一种性质；此处强调推测尚未验证。
annotations.example: Don't turn an assumption into a fact.

annotations.explain: split up 在此指车队分成不同路线，也可指情侣分手，依上下文辨义。
annotations.example: The group split up at the crossroads.

annotations.explain: head + 方位副词是常用旅行叙述，可直接说 head north，无需 to。
annotations.example: We headed east after lunch.

annotations.explain: toward 表示方向，不保证已经到达，与 to 的终点含义不同。
annotations.example: They walked toward the station.

annotations.explain: rise 为不及物动词，过去式 rose；abruptly 强调突兀。
annotations.example: He rose abruptly from the table.

annotations.explain: 表示两件事存在短暂时间差，与 after a while 相近。
annotations.example: She called back a little later.

annotations.explain: in place 指安排已就绪，all along 强调“从一开始就”。
annotations.example: The safeguards had been in place all along.

annotations.explain: after all 在这里修正先前评价，不是“毕竟”的唯一译法。
annotations.example: Maybe he was right after all.

annotations.explain: say something to someone's face 是常见表达，强调直接告知本人。
annotations.example: If you disagree, say it to his face.

annotations.explain: get out of + 名词/-ing 可表示设法不做不想做的事；区别于字面“从里面出来”。
annotations.example: He tried to get out of doing the dishes.

annotations.explain: paperwork 不可数，泛指填写、提交和处理各种文件。
annotations.example: The paperwork took all morning.

annotations.explain: could have + 过去分词谈过去未实现的可能情况，不表示真的回去了。
annotations.example: We could have left earlier.

annotations.explain: put out 除“发布”外常指熄灭灯火或扑灭火。
annotations.example: Please put out the candle before leaving.

annotations.explain: 用于叙事突然转折，but 和 just then 强化事件打断原计划。
annotations.example: But just then, the door opened.

annotations.explain: from the direction of 指来向，不等于起点已经确定在某地。
annotations.example: A shout came from the direction of the market.

annotations.explain: sleeve rode up 中 ride up 是衣物往上窜，不指骑马。
annotations.example: His sleeve rode up as he reached for the bag.

annotations.explain: knot A around B 表示把绳子等打结固定在某物周围。
annotations.example: She knotted a ribbon around the parcel.

annotations.explain: seize 比 take/hold 更突然有力，常暗示紧迫情绪。
annotations.example: He seized my hand to stop me.

annotations.explain: dig into 在此表示指甲用力压入，不是“开始吃”或“钻研”。
annotations.example: The bag's strap dug into my shoulder.

annotations.explain: 现在完成时 have been to 表示有过到某地的经历或到访，不意味着现在仍在那里。
annotations.example: She's been to Kyoto twice.

annotations.explain: the day before 指叙事参照日的前一天，不等同于 yesterday。
annotations.example: He had left the day before.

annotations.explain: 间接引语中的 was delivering 保留过去进行时的临时行动背景。
annotations.example: She said she was waiting outside.

annotations.explain: myself 用来强调亲身经历的缺失，为证言来源划清界限。
annotations.example: I never saw the document myself.

annotations.explain: have an urge to do 表示强烈冲动；a sudden urge to do 常见于第一人称叙述。
annotations.example: I had a sudden urge to call her.

annotations.explain: run after somebody 表示追着人跑，也可比喻一味追求某人某物。
annotations.example: She ran after the departing bus.

annotations.explain: before + 从句突出阻止发生在动作开始前。
annotations.example: He stopped me before I could speak.

annotations.explain: 独立短句用过去时提醒曾作出的承诺，具体承诺内容由上文推断。
annotations.example: You promised you wouldn't interfere.

annotations.explain: stop dead 是固定搭配，指突然完全停止，dead 在此作加强语气的副词。
annotations.example: She stopped dead when she heard the sound.

annotations.explain: casually 突出动作看似随意，point at 指动作指向的具体对象。
annotations.example: He casually pointed at the damaged wheel.

annotations.explain: with + 情绪名词可修饰说话或行动的方式。
annotations.example: She answered with obvious irritation.

annotations.explain: By the time 搭配过去时常描述两件过去事件的先后；主句状态在该时点已改变。
annotations.example: By the time he returned, the shop was empty.

annotations.explain: be gone 描写某物不再存在或可见，可用于人物表情。
annotations.example: The warmth in her voice was gone.

annotations.explain: hire 可指租用车辆或雇佣人员；区别于 buy。
annotations.example: We hired a van for the day.

annotations.explain: once 在此是时间连词“……之后”，不是“一次”。
annotations.example: Call me once the work is done.

annotations.explain: actually 可以表达出乎意料或核实，不总等于“实际上”。
annotations.example: Did he actually agree to that?

annotations.explain: instead of + -ing 表示取代关系，不能接动词原形。
annotations.example: We repaired it instead of replacing it.

annotations.explain: hurry to do 表示很快采取某个动作，常暗示辩解或紧张。
annotations.example: He hurried to explain the mistake.

annotations.explain: let slip something 指不经意泄露本想保留的信息。
annotations.example: She let slip the date of the surprise party.

annotations.explain: come through someone 表示经过某人之手或渠道，并不自动证明最终来源。
annotations.example: The payment had come through a broker.

annotations.explain: all those years ago 有回望久远往事的情感色彩。
annotations.example: We met all those years ago.

annotations.explain: nowhere near 可加强否定程度，表示离所需标准差得很远。
annotations.example: That is nowhere near enough information.

annotations.explain: justify 在此指能够为某种法律行动提供充分理由；不能由“有线索”直接推出“可逮捕”。
annotations.example: The rumor alone could not justify an arrest.

annotations.explain: push A toward B 表示沿某方向推动物体，动作可表现长辈的关照。
annotations.example: She pushed the plate toward him.

annotations.explain: get + 形容词表状态逐渐变化，常用进行时表示眼下变化。
annotations.example: The soup is getting cold.

annotations.explain: at a time like this 用于强调当前状况特殊，常带惊讶或不满。
annotations.example: Can you joke at a time like this?

annotations.explain: 动名词短语作句子主语，go hungry 表示没吃饭而挨饿。
annotations.example: Going hungry won't help you think clearly.

annotations.explain: bring back 指让某物回来，这里是否定夸张，意在提醒先照顾身体。
annotations.example: Nothing will bring that lost hour back.

annotations.explain: halfway through + 事件/时间 表示进行到中途。
annotations.example: Halfway through dinner, the phone rang.

annotations.explain: ride up 表示骑行接近某地点，through the rain 强调冒雨而来。
annotations.example: A messenger rode up through the storm.

annotations.explain: step out 是口语短语动词，强调暂时离开室内。
annotations.example: Could you step out for a moment?

annotations.explain: wear an expression 是习惯性比喻搭配，不是真的“穿戴表情”。
annotations.example: He was wearing a puzzled expression.

annotations.explain: send word 表示通知、托人传话，比 send a letter 更不限传递方式。
annotations.example: Please send word when you arrive.

annotations.explain: 现在完成时被动语态 have been + 过去分词强调跟踪行动已完成或有结果。
annotations.example: The vehicles have been followed since noon.

annotations.explain: have not been able to 表示迄今未具备能力或条件，不是已经查验而无发现。
annotations.example: We haven't been able to verify the records.

annotations.explain: do something for nothing 可表示劳动无成果，也可能指免费做事，须结合上下文。
annotations.example: We waited for hours for nothing.

annotations.explain: make a scene / there was a scene 指引人注目的争执或骚动。
annotations.example: There was a scene outside the station.

annotations.explain: turn oneself in 表示主动向执法机构自首，区别于被抓捕。
annotations.example: He decided to turn himself in.

annotations.explain: claim 标注某人自己的说法，作者不替该说法背书。
annotations.example: He claimed he had seen the driver.

annotations.explain: in front of 不只指空间前方，也表示公开目击的场合。
annotations.example: She made the announcement in front of a crowd.

annotations.explain: onlooker 指旁观事件的人，本身不意味着具备独立核验证据的能力。
annotations.example: Several onlookers recorded the incident.

annotations.explain: used to 表过去状态；work as 接职位，work for 接雇主。
annotations.example: She used to work as a clerk.

annotations.explain: rack one's brains 是高频惯用表达，意思是努力回想或思考。
annotations.example: I racked my brains for his name.

annotations.explain: come back to somebody 表示记忆重新浮现，否定句强调回忆失败。
annotations.example: The answer finally came back to me.

annotations.explain: come forward 常用于证人、知情人或志愿者主动提供信息。
annotations.example: Two witnesses came forward yesterday.

annotations.explain: according to 用于标明消息来源；来源可信度仍需单独判断。
annotations.example: According to the witness, the truck left at dawn.

annotations.phrase: How much of that is true
annotations.explain: how much of 表示整体中有多大部分，强调真实性尚未确认。
annotations.example: We don't know how much of the story is true.

annotations.explain: for + 名词 + to do 用于说明应由谁完成某行为；establish 指查证事实。
annotations.example: It's for the court to establish what happened.

annotations.explain: all at once 可表示“突然”，也可表示“同时”；此处是前者。
annotations.example: All at once, the room went quiet.

annotations.explain: as if 引出对神态的推测；weigh whether 是斟酌选择的文学表达。
annotations.example: She paused as if weighing whether to speak.

annotations.explain: in the end 强调考虑或变化后的最终结果，区别于 at the end（某事末尾）。
annotations.example: In the end, he told us the truth.

annotations.explain: order somebody to do 为动词搭配；had ordered 回溯三年前行为，并非已经证实命令存在。
annotations.example: She said the supervisor had ordered her to wait.

annotations.phrase: from three thousand shi to eight thousand
annotations.explain: from ... to ... 表数值变化；shi 是古代粮食计量单位，不可擅自换算成现代固定重量。
annotations.example: The total rose from ten to fifteen.

annotations.explain: without + -ing 可表示不假思索地完成动作，也可批评没考虑后果。
annotations.example: I answered without thinking.

annotations.explain: sit + 形容词可描述持续状态，motionless 指身体几乎无动作。
annotations.example: She sat motionless by the window.

annotations.explain: barely 表“仅仅、勉强”，above a whisper 描述音量仅略高于耳语。
annotations.example: His voice was barely above a whisper.

annotations.explain: back then 是口语常见时间表达，强调与现在相隔一段时期。
annotations.example: Back then, I didn't know what it meant.

annotations.explain: 助动词 did 在肯定句中强调事实，省略号表现迟疑；语气与普通 wrote 不同。
annotations.example: I did send the letter, but I never received a reply.

scenes.title: 赶回刑部报信
scenes.alt: 姜明月与温梨听阿芹急报，刑部门外有人往来；此图为报信的概括性呈现。

scenes.title: 顾怀川说明调查边界
scenes.alt: 刑部值房中，顾怀川向姜明月和温梨解释调查与搜查的权限界限。

scenes.alt: 月色下三辆灰篷运箱车从茶棚外经过，在路口向不同方向行驶。

scenes.title: 秦叔套出租车线索
scenes.alt: 秦叔佯作随意与车夫谈论车辕，姜明月与温梨留在茶棚内。

scenes.title: 马世全投案消息
scenes.alt: 雨夜茶棚里秦叔转述马世全当众声称投案的消息，温梨端着汤碗愣住。
